issues.body: `_Harness.__init__` calls `_require_script_tools()` before `_require_jq()`, while `_UNSTUBBED_SCRIPT_TOOLS` already contains `jq`. With jq missing, `_require_script_tools()` always raises first, so the new jq-specific diagnostic can never fire. `test_harness_refuses_to_run_without_jq` only checks generic substrings (`jq` present and two accusations absent), all of which the earlier sweep's message already satisfies; therefore the test remains green even if `_require_jq()` or its call is deleted. The comments/docstring claiming the jq-specific diagnosis is applied to every harness execution are not true on the real path.
issues.fix_hint: Use one authoritative precondition. Either fold the desired jq-specific diagnosis into `_require_script_tools()` and remove `_require_jq()`, or arrange dispatch so jq is handled by `_require_jq()` before/excluded from the generic sweep. Make the focused test distinguish the intended diagnostic (for example, assert a jq-specific phrase) and add a mutation-sensitive assertion such that removing the jq-specific path makes it fail. Update the nearby comments to describe the actual ordering.
issues.title: jq-specific precondition is unreachable and its test passes on the wrong exception

verdict.summary: The round-2 revision introduces a redundant jq-specific precondition after the existing declared-tool sweep, but the sweep already raises whenever jq is absent. Consequently `_require_jq()` is unreachable in exactly the condition it is meant to diagnose, and the new test is vacuous with respect to that load-bearing claim because it accepts the earlier generic AssertionError. This is a new major finding relative to round 1's clean approval, so progress is regressing.
